messages:
kai: quick heads-up — ran a 10m synthetic experiment simulating an edge split (50/25/25) across us-west / us-east / eu-west for the new mpt-7b-4q quant build. I wanted to see median vs tail and whether routing is blowing up p95 in any region. Results + command below.

maria: can you paste the exact exec and the fixture you used? was KV cache warm?

kai: command I used:```bash
./bench/run_bench --model mpt-7b-4q --regions us-west,us-east,eu-west \n  --edge-split 50,25,25 --duration 10m --rps 500 --seq-len 128 \n  --warmup 2m --capture-p50,p95,p99 --save results/edge-split.json
```
KV cache was cold for first minute, 2m warmup afterwards. batch size default (auto).

ben: raw summarized numbers from results/edge-split.json (median / 95th):
- us-east: p50 47ms, p95 210ms
- us-west: p50 55ms, p95 310ms
- eu-west: p50 118ms, p95 455ms
throughput sat at ~480 rps total before backpressure. H100 fleet, quant 4-bit.

aj: eu-west looks like two things: 1) extra network hop + higher RTT to nearest inference pool, 2) kernel fallback on long-ish KV misses causing slower per-token kernels. we saw that when seq-len distribution skewed >120 it picked scalar fallback.

sre-liaison: confirmed — edge gateways in eu-west are NATting to a different pop (+4-7ms median) and the proxy chain sometimes adds +50-100ms tail under load. we have a ticket to reduce proxy hops but that's medium priority.

aj: quick repro: force the newer quant kernel and reduce dynamic batching to avoid kernel fallback:```bash
export REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=quant_v2
./bench/run_bench --model mpt-7b-4q --regions eu-west --rps 200 --seq-len 128 --batch-max 16 --warmup 3m
```
There was a config bug where batch-max defaulted to 64 in eu-west.

ops-bot: deploy 1994556770 -> bench-configs/edge-split updated by kai :white_check_mark:

maria: re-ran with kernel override + 3m warmup + batch-max 16 in eu-west. new numbers:
- eu-west: p50 105ms, p95 375ms (p95 improved ~80ms)
- us-west: unchanged p50 53ms, p95 290ms
- us-east: p50 45ms, p95 200ms
Also warmed prefix cache for 30s reduces eu-west p95 another ~20ms on some runs.

ben: note on quality — mpt-7b-4q shows a small uptick in stop-token hallucination (~0.8% -> 1.4%) vs 8-bit baseline on our eval set. for customer-facing EU traffic maybe run 8-bit canary until we tune quant decoder.

kai: thanks. proposed next steps: 1) schedule 2h canary in eu-west routing 10% traffic to 8-bit variant, 2) enable kernel force on eu-west infra for the 4q bucket while we patch batch-max default, 3) add a tracing tag to measure proxy hop latency per request to quantify network tail.

sre-liaison: I'll open the proxy hop tracing ticket and add a short dashboard.

maria: I'll prep the canary plan + rollback steps. can we do the canary tomorrow morning at 08:00 UTC?

kai: yep. tagging @sre-liaison and @ben for followups. :thumbsup:
